investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit is 100)
investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for remote-agent-create (and all sibling checks remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime) failed because POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", meaning the eval service account's org has reached the maximum allowed swarm agent count. The eval probe never created an agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected and all contract assertions were unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend rejected the eval's agent creation request with a hard quota conflict (HTTP 409, code: "conflict", message: "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100"). The org used by the observability probe has accumulated 100 swarm agents — the enforced ceiling — leaving no capacity for the eval to provision a new remote agent. Because agent creation is the first step in the runner branch (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1339: createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)), all three remote-agents checks fail at the same upstream boundary before any evidence can be written. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by quota exhaustion in the probe org; no user-traffic or production incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: POST /api/agents failed with 409 — error body contains 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the swarm backend enforced a hard cap and rejected the creation request.

sibling.remote-agent-state and sibling.remote-agent-runtime both carry the identical 409 message (sameMessage: true), confirming all three checks share the same upstream failure point at agent creation.

failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), confirming the runner never reached the evidence-writing stage.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1331-1339: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after requireOrgId — a 409 at this call would abort the entire withCleanup block before any evidence is recorded.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:178-186: contract requires vmIdPresent === true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because agent creation never succeeded.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1155 — the request returned in ~1 second, consistent with an immediate quota-rejection response rather than a timeout or VM provisioning delay.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Probe org has reached the swarm agent quota ceiling of 100: prior eval runs or other automation created agents that were not cleaned up (withCleanup may have failed silently or been skipped), leaving stale agents consuming quota slots. This is directly stated in the 409 error body (failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — The withCleanup mechanism in the runner failed to delete agents from previous eval runs, causing quota to accumulate over time. The runner branch (run-status-probes.mjs line 1337) wraps creation in withCleanup, but if cleanup was interrupted (e.g., CI job cancellation, network error during teardown) agents would persist.
TERTIARY — A separate automated process or manual action in the probe org created a large number of remote agents independently of the eval runner, consuming available quota before the eval ran.

LOW CONFIDENCE — Commit 5a0475f ('fix(observability): stabilize status freshness signals', committed 2026-06-16T14:26:04Z, ~22 minutes before the eval ran) touched eval infrastructure files including .github/workflows/aura-observability.yml and aura-observability-repair.yml. It is possible a workflow change altered cleanup behavior or scheduling, but the commit's candidateTouchedPaths list is empty and no matched needles link it to the quota or cleanup logic. This remains a hypothesis only (suspect-change.5a0475f, confidence: low).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit is 100)
investigations.summary: The AURA observability eval for remote-agent-create (and all sibling checks remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime) failed because POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", meaning the eval service account's org has reached the maximum allowed swarm agent count. The eval probe never created an agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected and all contract assertions were unverifiable.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend rejected the eval's agent creation request with a hard quota conflict (HTTP 409, code: "conflict", message: "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100"). The org used by the observability probe has accumulated 100 swarm agents — the enforced ceiling — leaving no capacity for the eval to provision a new remote agent. Because agent creation is the first step in the runner branch (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1339: createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)), all three remote-agents checks fail at the same upstream boundary before any evidence can be written. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by quota exhaustion in the probe org; no user-traffic or production incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1155 — the request returned in ~1 second, consistent with an immediate quota-rejection response rather than a timeout or VM provisioning delay.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Probe org has reached the swarm agent quota ceiling of 100: prior eval runs or other automation created agents that were not cleaned up (withCleanup may have failed silently or been skipped), leaving stale agents consuming quota slots. This is directly stated in the 409 error body (failed-check.message).

The runner branch (run-status-probes.mjs line 1337) wraps creation in withCleanup, but if cleanup was interrupted (e.g., CI job cancellation, network error during teardown) agents would persist.
TERTIARY — A separate automated process or manual action in the probe org created a large number of remote agents independently of the eval runner, consuming available quota before the eval ran.

LOW CONFIDENCE — Commit 5a0475f ('fix(observability): stabilize status freshness signals', committed 2026-06-16T14:26:04Z, ~22 minutes before the eval ran) touched eval infrastructure files including .github/workflows/aura-observability.yml and aura-observability-repair.yml.
